description: Urban Tree Monitoring: A Resource Guide sets out standard protocols for designing and running projects that follow individual urban trees over time, for example to measure survival, growth and condition. Natalie van Doorn, Lara Roman, Gregory McPherson and fourteen co-authors published it in 2020 as General Technical Report PSW-GTR-266 of the USDA Forest Service Pacific Southwest Research Station, as a companion to Urban Tree Monitoring: A Field Guide. Part I covers monitoring goals, the development of the standards, project types, links to other urban tree protocols, recording tree locations and identifiers, databases, data collection systems, research-practice partnerships, crew training and fieldwork; Part II defines five data sets, the Minimum, Tree, Site, Young Tree Management and Community data sets, with study goals and variables; Part III has appendices. Coverage is US urban forestry practice, usable elsewhere. Format and access: a free 132-page PDF. Licence: US federal public domain. Caveats: it defines what to collect and holds no data. It standardises the tree condition data that climate adaptation and capacity planning models of urban green infrastructure need. Related catalogue records are the US Forest Service Urban FIA and the ISA pre- and post-storm urban forest data protocol.
